title: Compute brief - 23 November 2026
description: Washington is redrawing where compute can sit. Trump threatened a tremendous tax on US companies that build data centres abroad, the BIS rule stalled server and foundry shipments across Asia, and Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang after input from senior US officials. Wire: US offshore threat, TSMC holds, Southeast Asia server halt, Huang back, Applied Digital 150 MW, Alberta Bill 42, Greece Kozani, India L&T B300, Indonesia Firmus bond, New Zealand Stratford. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Build it here, or pay: Washington moves the map.
lede: President Trump said on 20 November that the US will not allow its companies to build data centres abroad, or will put a tremendous tax on them if they do; no rate, scope or legal authority was given and nothing has been published. The BIS remote-access rule that took effect on 19 November is already biting: Nikkei reports at least two Nvidia server partners halted shipments to Southeast Asia and TSMC held some shipments to Chinese and non-Chinese designers while it checks the new 16nm and 14nm presumption. On 23 November Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, eleven days after he resigned, saying senior US government officials gave input that he poses no national security risk. Demand is not slowing at home: Applied Digital signed a 150 MW, 18-year hyperscaler lease at higher pricing. List prices held for an eleventh day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.

watch.name: Offshore data centre penalty
watch.note: Watch for an executive order, Treasury guidance or a bill; Congress holds the taxing power and IEEPA tariffs were struck down in February.

watch.note: Jensen Huang sits for transcribed interviews with three House committees on 1 December; general counsel Tim Teter on 2 December. Nvidia's independent investigation continues.
